Heating and cooling energy consumption 15-minute time-series data before and after the attic floor insulation upgrade for the example unit in Texas 14 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4.3 Stock Energy Impact Out of 550,000 units, 235,950 units are applicable for attic floor insulation upgrades (42.9%). For the 235,950 applicable units, the total baseline consumption is 3,454 TWh per year. After the attic floor insulation upgrade, the total consumption is reduced to 3,377 TWh per year or a 2.2% reduction. Figure 8 shows that energy savings from attic floor insulation primarily come from heating and cooling related end uses, with 3.9% electricity heating savings (10 TWh), 3.7% natural gas heating savings (42 TWh), 2.4% electricity cooling savings (9.4 B kWh), and 2.4% cooling fan and pump energy savings (2.0 TWh). Energy savings were observed only in heating and cooling end uses, while other end uses like lighting and appliances remained unchanged. This is because attic insulation upgrades affect thermal performance by reducing heat loss in winter and heat gain in summer, which directly impacts space conditioning loads. Savings from heating is higher than cooling because heating seasons are generally longer and more severe than cooling seasons across most U.S. climate zones. Figure 8.
